summary: Neighborhood associations and community groups in the city have been running a tree-planting drive since September 15, 2023, turning vacant lots and barren parks into green spaces to fight climate change. The article highlights leaders, the role of technology like an AI planting app, the Beacon Project's green corridors, and school involvement through Green Shoots. It also covers funding and weather challenges and speculates on future tech such as autonomous planting vehicles.
one_line: Community tree-planting drives led by neighborhood associations, volunteers, schools and startups are greening the city and exploring technology to support urban forestry.
key_facts: The neighborhood tree-planting program began on September 15, 2023, following international calls for increased urban forestry.
Jamie Richardson is president of the Maplewood Neighborhood Association and a leader of the tree-planting drive.
Dr. Lakshmi Gupta is a noted botanist and community activist who joined the effort.
Startup Sow the Future is testing an AI-powered app that guides volunteers on where to plant based on historical climate patterns and projected urban development.
Alex Moritz, a tech entrepreneur and local resident, is collaborating on a project to monitor tree health remotely, described as 'a Fitbit for trees'.
Drones for aerial mapping and soil sensors measuring moisture and pH levels are expected to help identify planting locations and track conditions.
The Beacon Project, led by retired school teacher Regina Hall, aims to link neighborhoods through green corridors so animals and insects can migrate safely.
The Beacon Project also hosts workshops on sustainability and ecology.
The Green Shoots program pairs classroom learning with hands-on gardening and planting activities in local schools.
Trevor Nash, a local science teacher, says students are seeing photosynthesis and the water cycle in action.
Challenges include unpredictable weather patterns, urban development pressures, and funding deficits.
Richardson says funding has come from crowdfunding campaigns, local sponsorships, and in-kind donations from local nurseries.
Future technologies mentioned include autonomous planting vehicles, biodegradable planting drones, and enhanced genetic selection for hardier tree species.
